verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both clauses are stated, but as two declarations rather than one display, and with one extra conclusion. The dictionary is X_a = NominalConeAssembly.activeLeft W, X_- = zeroEnd W H lo, X_+ = nominalOuterX W, X_b = NominalConeAssembly.activeRight W = Real.exp (ConstructedSlowBase.activeRight W) (by `exp_right_eq_cone`); the paper's ordering X_a < X_- < X_+ < X_b is `window_order` (activeLeft < zeroEnd), `zeroEnd_lt_outer`, and `ConstructedSlowBase.outer_before_upper` (nominalOuterX < activeUpper = exp activeRight). First clause: `modulated_positive_radialSupport` is stated for every n ≥ 1 with the wider right endpoint X_b, so at n = 1 it is exactly supp_X 𝒯_1 ⊂ [X_-, X_b]. Second clause: `aligned_higher_support` (and `modulatedCoefficients H v` is by definition `alignedCoefficients W H v.profiles v.finiteModification …`) gives, for n ≥ 2, tsupport ⊆ Icc X_- X_+ ×ˢ Icc (-outer) outer — the paper's [X_-, X_+], and in addition it confines the η-support, where the paper only says the radial supports are uniform over |η| ≤ 1. The paper's single symbol 𝒯_n is the pair (𝒯_{n,θ}, 𝒯_{n,z}) of (5.9); the Lean carries the two components as `stressTheta n` and `stressAxial n` and states each conjunct separately. One encoding point: `radialSupport` says the field vanishes off Icc a b, whereas `aligned_higher_support` bounds the closure of the support; both give supp_X ⊆ [X_-, ·].
